name: b-crosshatched-grin-closeup
prompt: A tall portrait black-and-white ink drawing on off-white paper: a fat, wealthy gentleman's face pressed so close it fills the whole frame from side to side, nothing behind him but paper. The brim of his black top hat slices straight across the top edge, and under it his brow and both eye sockets are built from layer upon layer of fine crossed pen lines until they sink to near-black, the hatching thinning toward the cheeks into tiny stipple dots like pores. Out of that darkness one eye glistens, wet and too detailed, rendered with far more care than the rest of the face; in the small white highlight of that eye, curved by the eyeball, sits a minute reflection of a hospital nurse in rumpled scrubs slumped on a park bench, the only other person in the picture. Below, his cheeks swell into a smile that is courteous and much too wide, stretching nearly ear to ear, lips thin, a row of small even teeth, the corners pushed up into fleshy folds of hatched jowl. The pen work is obsessive and slightly scratchy, short broken strokes that change direction across the skin, the scratch of the nib visible, the white of the paper kept clean only in the eye's highlight, the teeth and the collar. The bottom fifth of the frame below his jowls and starched collar fades into bare untouched paper. Flat frontal camera at eye level, lens close enough to feel uncomfortable, even shadowless light so all the darkness comes from ink alone. Pure black ink and paper white, no grey wash, no colour, no lettering or text anywhere. Thanks.
